postImages.source: Owner decision (2026-10-18): each post's own image from Webflow (already its Sanity mainImage) comes back on the blog pages only when it is a real photo, stock or the crew's, at least 1,200 px wide, and not AI-made, not text or drawn-on effects, not of unknown source and not misleading (seo-audit PLAN section 8, "If yes"; each image looked at). `shown` sets post.showMainImage and the image's alt (what is visible; a stock photo's alt never implies the people in it work for us). Each shown entry names its `image` (the asset the post's main image must be: the pipeline fails if the post's image changes, so a swapped image is decided again) and, for stock, its `name` (the file name on Sanity's CDN, which web/src/lib/image-names.ts reads from here; what is visible, never the business or the crew). A `company` entry's image must be one of the company's photos (web/src/lib/library-photos.json or web/src/lib/brand-photos.ts); its file name stays where that photo is named. `notShown` says why the others keep a company photo. Every post is in exactly one list. Service and city pages never show these images.

postQuickAnswers.source: post.quickAnswer: the "Quick answer" box above a post's body (CONTENT_MODEL: 40–60 words, answer first). Without one the box shows the post's excerpt, which is its live meta description; on these seven posts that excerpt repeats, or restates, the opening sentence the box sits right above (visual-posts F1, 2026-10-18), or is no answer at all. Each answer sums up what the post itself says: every `evidence` phrase must appear word for word in the post body as it ships (quote style ignored), and no answer may carry a price. The migration also stops if any post's box would repeat its opening.

why-does-my-breaker-keep-tripping-in-the.text: In a Phoenix summer a breaker usually trips for one of four reasons: overloaded circuits, an old or undersized panel, connections loosened by heat, or a failing A/C compressor or motor that draws too much current on startup. Have the A/C checked, and if tripping is frequent, have a licensed electrician check your panel, circuits, and wiring.
evidence: Extreme heat causes metal to expand and contract
A failing compressor or motor in your HVAC system can draw too much current on startup
If tripping is frequent, it’s time to have a licensed electrician check your panel, circuits, and wiring

why-your-lights-flicker.text: A brief dim when the AC or another large appliance starts up is normal. Flickering that happens often, shows in several rooms at once or comes every time the AC runs usually points to loose panel connections, aging breakers, overloaded or unbalanced circuits, deteriorating wiring or grounding issues, and it tends to get worse in summer.
evidence: brief, slight dimming when a large appliance starts up, especially an air conditioner
flicker in multiple rooms at once
loose connections in the panel, aging breakers, overloaded or unbalanced circuits, deteriorating wiring, or grounding issues
Why Flickering Often Gets Worse in Summer

breaker-trips-ac.text: It is rarely the AC itself. Its startup surge finds the weak spot in your electrical system: an older or weakened breaker, an undersized panel, a shared or overloaded circuit, wiring issues behind the walls, or poor grounding and load balance. If the breaker trips more than once under normal use, have a licensed electrician inspect the system.
evidence: This usually isn’t an AC problem
If a breaker trips more than once under normal use

common-electrical-issues-in-scottsdale-h.text: Scottsdale's heat, haboob dust and monsoon power surges are hard on electrical systems, and older homes may still have outdated wiring. Watch for flickering lights, frequently tripped breakers, dead outlets, buzzing and burning smells. If you smell burning, turn off power to that area and call a licensed electrician right away.
evidence: Scottsdale's intense heat stresses electrical systems
powerful dust storms known as haboobs
Older homes in Scottsdale may still have outdated wiring
If you smell burning, turn off power to that area and call a licensed electrician right away

do-you-need-an-electrical-panel-upgrade-.text: Your home likely needs a panel upgrade if it still has a fuse box or a Zinsco or Federal Pacific panel, if you are adding a hot tub, EV charger or new HVAC system, if breakers keep tripping, if you notice flickering lights or buzzing sounds, or if the house is 30+ years old. Most upgrades take one day.
evidence: a fuse box or an older panel brand like Zinsco or Federal Pacific

how-phoenix-heat-affects-your-homes-elec.text: Heat makes wiring expand by day and contract at night, which loosens connections and can cause arcing. Peak AC and pool pump loads overload breakers, and UV cracks outdoor wire insulation. Watch for breakers tripping in the afternoon, lights dimming when the AC starts, burning smells and warped outlet covers, and schedule a summer electrical inspection.

emfs-in-your-phoenix-home.text: EMFs are a normal part of using electricity. The concern is unusually strong readings near certain walls or floors, often with buzzing outlets or flickering lights, which usually point to wiring defects, grounding problems or load issues. A licensed electrician finds the cause and corrects it with grounding and bonding work, load balancing or a panel upgrade.
